title: Embedding pipeline smoothing: adaptive ingress reshuffle and kernel hotpath tuning
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Problem: Several customers report intermittent 99th-percentile latency spikes on the embeddings endpoint during variable load patterns. Root-cause signals from telemetry point to three contributing factors: (1) ingress request batching variance causing microbursts that prevent steady batch formation; (2) kernel hotpath contention for small vs large microbatches when quantized kernels are selected suboptimally; (3) cold KV-cache and prefill jitter for repeated short requests. Goal: Reduce p99 by 30% and p95 by 15% while keeping p50 stable and not increasing cost >5% through a combination of adaptive ingress reshuffle, microbatch-sizing policy, and selective kernel hotpath tuning including a lightweight quantized fallback. Approach: 1) Implement an ingress reshuffle dispatcher that reorders inflight embedding requests into size-aware buckets for a short, bounded window (<=5ms) to reduce variance in per-inference batch sizes. 2) Add a microbatch-sizing policy that adapts target microbatch size by observed sequence length distribution and tenant priority, exposing a tunable knob for Dedicated customers. 3) Introduce a kernel hotpath hint: the scheduler will choose kernel variants based on an observed microbatch size histogram; add a fast-path for very small batches to use a minimal-kernel to avoid contention. 4) Prefill KV-cache heuristics: opportunistic warmup of frequently accessed KV prefixes on repeated requests and a lightweight prefetch probe for cold clients. 5) Rollout with experiment flags, collect tail-focused telemetry, and run canary on a subset of tenants (low-risk then ramp). This ticket covers design, implementation, experiments, and rollout plan for the reshuffle + kernel hinting changes; follow-up tickets will handle autoscaling changes and Dedicated autoscaling tuning.
acceptance_criteria: p99 embeddings endpoint latency reduced by >=30% relative to 2026-02-15 baseline for mixed short/long sequence workload
p95 reduced by >=15% for same workload
no more than 5% increase in per-token compute cost on average across test tenants
unit tests and integration tests for reshuffle dispatcher and kernel-hint path added
canary rollout completes without elevated error rates (>0.5% regression) or SLA violations
observability: new dashboard broken down by batch-size buckets, kernel-variant, and tenant; heatmap of prefill hit rate

updates: 2026-02-28 - Arjun Patel: Created ticket, attached initial telemetry snapshots and heatmap of batch-size variance. Noted correlation between ingress bursts and kernel contention events.

2026-03-03 - Maya Thompson: Implemented prototype of bounded ingress window in local cluster; preliminary results show 18% p99 reduction for synthetic short-heavy workload. Added unit tests for dispatcher ordering.
2026-03-06 - Ravi Desai: Added kernel hotpath hint prototype; small-batch minimal-kernel reduces lock contention in microbench by 25% median CPU time. Need perf runs on 4090 and A100.
2026-03-10 - Yuna Kim: KV prefill heuristic prototype implemented; observed 12% hit-rate improvement for repeated short clients in staging. Will combine with reshuffle in next run.

2026-03-12 - Arjun Patel: Ran combined canary on 5% of production tenants for 12 hours. Observed p99 down 24% and p95 down 13% vs baseline; cost +2.1%. Noted two tenants with traffic patterns that increased p99 due to bursty long-sequence requests - opened follow-up investigation.
risks: Bounded ingress delay can add steady-state latency for very latency-sensitive clients if misconfigured
Kernel hinting may cause regressions on specialized hardware if kernel selection logic misclassifies microbatch sizes
Prefill heuristics might increase memory and GPU cache pressure under large-tenant workloads
Complexity in scheduler may interact with existing autoscaler behavior - need SRE validation
